intro.title: Backspace String Compare
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that compares two strings after applying backspace operations, where the '#' character deletes the previous character. You will learn the core concept of using a stack data structure to process strings character by character, simulating the backspace effect. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays (acting as stacks) and string iteration with loops. This beginner-friendly exercise will help you understand how to manipulate and compare data structures efficiently.
intro.usecase: The Backspace String Compare pattern is essential for validating user input in text editors, code editors, and form fields where backspace/delete functionality is present. Developers implement this when building features like real-time document comparison in collaborative tools (Google Docs, VS Code Live Share) or validating typed commands in terminal emulators. It's also used in password managers that compare partially typed passwords with stored ones, and in search interfaces that process user queries with corrections before executing searches. Understanding this algorithm helps developers handle user input sequences accurately across various interactive applications.
